newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila, Hanoi to discuss development of Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: Manila, Hanoi to discuss development of Spratlys.

text.p: Philippine and Vietnamese officials will meet in Hanoi next month to discuss how claimants to the disputed South China Sea islands could jointly develop the area, the Manila government said on Wednesday.

Departing Vietnamese ambassador Vu Quang Diem told President Fidel Ramos during a farewell call that his government was busy preparing to ensure the meeting's success, a presidential palace statement said.

It said Ramos asked the envoy to reiterate to Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet a Manila formula to settle conflicting claims over the islands and that he had presented a similar proposal to Chinese President Jiang Zemin last month.
The statement did not give details about the Manila proposal.

The potentially oil-rich Spratly Islands in the South China Sea are claimed wholly or in part by China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei. China and Vietnam have also staked claims on the Paracel islands adjacent to the Spratlys.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon will lead the Philippine panel to the Hanoi meeting which will form part of regular talks of the Philippines-Vietnam Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation.
The commission will also discuss bilateral trade.
